newsitem.title: FRANCE: French troops to start pullout of Congo.
newsitem.headline: French troops to start pullout of Congo.

text.p: French troops will start pulling out of Brazzaville on Sunday after ending the evacuation of French nationals from the strife-torn Congolese capital, the French Foreign Ministry said on Friday.

It said the evacuation would end on Sunday at 1600 GMT, when "the French military contingent will begin its disengagement with a view to a total pullout". France has more than 1,250 soldiers in Brazzaville.
A Ministry spokesman said all French troops would be withdrawn, but did not say how long the pullout would take. "There will not be any French troops left in the Congo," he said.

France despatched some 850 reinforcements, with six light tanks, to back up its 400 soldiers in Brazzaville as fighting between the forces of President Pascal Lissouba and former Marxist president Denis Sassou Nguesso intensified.

The French troops, operating out of Brazzaville airport and making forays into the city to rescue endangered foreigners, have flown 3,420 foreign civilians, 1,410 of them French, out of the country since "Operation Pelican" began on June 7.
The Foreign Ministry said all French nationals who wanted to be evacuated will have been flown out by Sunday.
